- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- github-morning-reporter: Use this agent when the user requests a morning report, daily summary, or overview of their GitHub activity. Trigger phrases include 'morning report', 'github report', 'daily github summary', 'what's happening on github', or 'check my github status'. This agent should be used proactively when the user starts their day or explicitly asks for repository updates.

Examples:
- User: "get me my morning github report"
  Assistant: "I'll use the github-morning-reporter agent to generate your comprehensive GitHub status report."
  <uses Agent tool to invoke github-morning-reporter>

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qa-agent: A static pre-ship audit. Invoke it right before shipping, opening a PR, or merging — or when the user explicitly asks "does this pass QA?". It reads the diff and returns PASS or BLOCK with specific findings. It reviews and reports; it never edits code. Examples:

Use when asked to "fix error handling", "find anti-patterns", "error handling audit", "silent catch", "swallowed errors", or "anti-pattern cleanup". Proactively suggest when the user mentions silent failures, empty catches, or debugging nightmares caused by swallowed errors.
- chroma: Open-source embedding database for AI applications. Store embeddings and metadata, perform vector and full-text search, filter by metadata. Simple 4-function API. Scales from notebooks to production clusters. Use for semantic search, RAG applications, or document retrieval. Best for local development and open-source projects.
- competitor-analysis: Run a competitor analysis against claude-mem. Clones a competitor repo, researches it deeply, pulls claude-mem context from mem-search, writes a detailed comparison report, and publishes to cmem-discussions.
- product-analysis: Deep-dive analysis of any product, project, or tool. Clones the repo, researches it thoroughly, pulls claude-mem context from mem-search, writes a detailed analysis of what it is and how it relates to claude-mem, and publishes to cmem-discussions.
- standup: Convene the recently-active git worktrees as named agents in a markdown group
chat, have them reconcile what each changed, and converge on ONE consolidated
worktree. Each branch is an agent that posts to a shared STANDUP.md (YAML front
matter holds the GOAL + PROMPT; the body is the chat log), then the room agrees
on a merge order and a single consolidation plan in the SUMMATION. The room is
filled either by time window (past 1h / 4h / 24h / 7d / all — only worktrees
active in it join, so a 40-worktree machine collapses to the handful you
actually touched) or by hand-picking specific worktrees and/or open GitHub PRs
from a checkbox-style list. Use this skill whenever the user says "standup",

One-shot report, does not apply fixes.

- ponytail:ponytail-gain: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, more speed, from the benchmark medians. One-shot display, not a persistent mode, and not a per-repo number. Trigger: /ponytail-gain, "ponytail gain", "what does ponytail save", "show ponytail impact", "ponytail scoreboard".
- ponytail:ponytail-help: Quick-reference card for all ponytail modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "what ponytail commands", "how do I use ponytail".
- ponytail:ponytail-review: Code review focused exclusively on over-engineering. Finds what to delete: reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, dead flexibility. One line per finding: location, what to cut, what replaces it. Use when the user says "review for over-engineering", "what can we delete", "is this over-engineered", "simplify review", or invokes /ponytail-review. Complements correctness-focused review, this one only hunts complexity.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

{"method":"get_file","path":"_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/readme.md","content":"# cmem viewer — Design System

**cmem viewer modern** is an app for *knowing and understanding* yourself through your records: memories, observations, and work history. It treats your accumulated context as something to browse, search, and reflect on — the way a marketplace treats jobs and people.

This design system was built from 14 UI screenshots (Mobbin captures of a modern talent-marketplace web app) supplied in `uploads/`. The visual language was studied from those references and re-expressed as an **original system** for cmem viewer — no third-party logos, names, or proprietary assets are reproduced.

**Sources**
- `uploads/Braintrust Web *.png` — 14 reference screenshots (home, feed, spaces, modals, forms, messaging, talent lists). Reference only; not shipped assets.
- No codebase or Figma was provided. Everything here is authored fresh against the reference language.

---

## CONTENT FUNDAMENTALS

**Voice: a warm, direct guide.** The product speaks *to you* about *your* memory. Always second person ("Your newest observations", "Where will your attention go today?"), first person only in user-authored content.

**Casing:** Sentence case everywhere — headings, buttons, tabs, badges ("Browse memories", "Save and continue", "Looking for patterns"). Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS (except tiny meta-labels are still sentence case).

**Greeting pattern:** big, personal, punctuated — `Hi, Alex!` as a display-size page title. Friendly exclamation marks are used sparingly but deliberately ("Click the link in your email!").

**Microcopy is task-shaped, not clever.** Buttons name the outcome: "Save my availability", "View all memories", "Earn today" → for cmem: "Open timeline", "Review this week". Helper text is one plain sentence below the control ("By default, we assume you work in your location's timezone.").

**Questions as headers.** Forms ask in plain language: "What is your hourly rate for this job?" → cmem: "When did this happen?", "Who was involved?". Required state is a quiet gray "Required" suffix, not an asterisk alone.

**Emoji: only inside tinted topic badges** (💪 Freelancing, 🔥 Asking for 1:1 help) — one leading emoji, never in headings, body copy, or buttons. cmem equivalents: 🧠 Insight, 📌 Observation, 🗂 Work history.

**Numbers are celebrated quietly:** "2103 members", "Your profile is 10% complete", "38 new posts last week". Stats are inline with icons, not stat-card grids.

**Example strings (cmem voice):**
- "Hi, Alex!"
- "Welcome to cmem. You now have full access to your timeline of memories, observations, and work history. Where will your attention go today?"
- "Your newest observations"
- "Ask your memory a question..."
- "Big news from October! You shipped the viewer redesign."

---

## VISUAL FOUNDATIONS

**Canvas & surfaces.** App background is a lavender-tinted off-white (`--canvas #f6f4fb`); content lives on pure white cards (`--paper`). Depth comes from this canvas/card contrast plus hairline borders — shadows are nearly absent (cards: `--shadow-card`, barely visible; modals: one large soft `--shadow-modal`).

**Ink-first actions.** The primary button is a **black pill** with white text. Color is reserved for meaning: jade green for affirmative commits ("Save and continue"), violet for selection/toggles, red only for destruction. Secondary buttons are white pills with a hairline border; disabled is gray fill, muted text.

**Pastel tint family.** Lilac, mint, peach, butter, sky (`--lilac-100`, `--mint-100`, …) used for: feature/hero tint cards, topic badges, active nav pill (lilac-200), space banners, skill chips. Tint cards carry **oversized soft geometric arc shapes** in a darker step of the same tint (200-level), bleeding off the card corner — the system's signature decorative motif. Never gradients.

**Type.** One family — Signat (see Fonts) — at 400/500/600/700/800. Hierarchy by size jump: display 56 → h1 40 → h2 28 → h3 20 → body 16 → small 14 → micro 12. Display/headers tracked slightly tight (−0.01 to −0.02em). Body line-height 1.5.

**Radii.** Pill-forward: buttons, badges, chips, search bar, nav items are full pills (`--radius-pill`). Cards 16px, hero cards & modals 20px, inputs 12px, thumbnails 12px.

**Borders.** Hairlines everywhere (`--line-1 #e8e6f0` on white, `--line-2` on inputs). Dashed borders (`--line-dashed`) mark empty/incomplete profile sections.

**Hover / press.** Hover: background shifts one step (white → canvas; canvas → canvas-deep) or border darkens line-1 → line-2; black buttons lighten to `#2c2c32`. Press: darken + no scale tricks. Transitions 120–200ms, `--ease-out`, no bounce, no parallax.

**Layout.** Fixed left sidebar (240–280px) with icon+label pill nav; fixed top bar with centered pill search; content column max ~1180px with generous 32–48px gutters. Modals are centered white sheets (max-width ~880px, radius 20px) over a 40% ink scrim. Toasts/banners: full-width black bar (top) with white text + underlined link.

**Avatars.** Circles. Navy fill (`--navy-700`) with white initials when no photo. Sizes 32 / 40 / 56 / 96.

**Imagery.** Photographic imagery is rare and neutral-warm; UI relies on tints + arcs instead. No illustration system in the reference set — do not invent one.

**Transparency & blur.** Not used. Surfaces are opaque; the scrim is flat alpha-ink.

---

## ICONOGRAPHY

The reference uses a consistent **1.5px-stroke outline icon set** (rounded caps, ~20–24px optical size): home, briefcase, chat bubble, wallet, bell, bookmark, envelope, search, calendar, location pin, globe, link, paperclip.

- **System icons:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) via CDN — closest open match in stroke weight and roundness. Load: `<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@latest"></script>` then `lucide.createIcons()`, or copy individual SVGs. Default: 20px, `stroke-width: 1.75`, `currentColor`.
- **Brand mark:** `assets/logo.svg` (wordmark + ring mark), `assets/logo-mark.svg` — original cmem marks, simple geometry.
- **Emoji:** only as leading glyphs in topic badges (see Content Fundamentals).
- **No icon font, no PNG icons, no unicode-as-icon.**

SUBSTITUTION FLAG: reference iconography appears custom; Lucide at stroke 1.75 is a visual stand-in. Provide brand SVGs to replace.

---

## Fonts

Brand font: **Signat**, self-hosted (.otf in `assets/fonts/`) via `@font-face` in `tokens/fonts.css`, weights 400/500/600/700/800 + regular italic. **Spline Sans Mono** (Google Fonts) for timestamps/IDs.

---

## INDEX

- `styles.css` — global entry; imports everything in `tokens/`.
- `tokens/` — `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css` (radii/shadows/motion), `fonts.css`, `base.css`.
- `guidelines/` — foundation specimen cards (rendered in the Design System tab).
- `assets/` — `logo.svg`, `logo-mark.svg`.
- `components/`
  - `actions/` — **Button**, **IconButton**
  - `forms/` — **Input**, **SearchBar**, **Checkbox**, **Switch**, **ChoiceChip**
  - `display/` — **Badge**, **Avatar**, **TintCard**
  - `navigation/` — **Tabs**, **NavItem**, **TopBar**
  - `feedback/` — **Modal**, **Banner**
- `ui_kits/cmem_viewer/` — interactive recreation of the product: home, timeline, collections, search; `index.html` is click-through.
- `SKILL.md` — agent skill entry point.

import json, base64, os

fonts_dir = os.path.join(out_dir, 'fonts')
os.makedirs(fonts_dir, exist_ok=True)

font_files = {
    'toolu_019tJwR8dibUYdKFQ7UApXSj.txt': 'Signat-regular.otf',
    'toolu_01KMsSp36MgvbZYHTCwskswu.txt': 'Signat-regularitalic.otf',

    'toolu_01EfMqbDHzjjWRwAmXaYWaPy.txt': 'Signat-semibold.otf',
    'toolu_0135PUvo7otNuW84v5RWk2xd.txt': 'Signat-bold.otf',
    'toolu_01ULzDTVY8XGKPxFBh6fXUWm.txt': 'Signat-extrabold.otf',
}
for src, name in font_files.items():
    data = json.load(open(os.path.join(results_dir, src)))
    assert data.get('isBase64') or True
    raw = base64.b64decode(data['content'])
    path = os.path.join(fonts_dir, name)
    open(path, 'wb').write(raw)
    # sanity: OTF magic
    magic = raw[:4]
    print(name, len(raw), 'bytes, magic:', magic)
EOF

input.content:
# cmem viewer — Design System

**cmem viewer modern** is an app for *knowing and understanding* yourself through your records: memories, observations, and work history. It treats your accumulated context as something to browse, search, and reflect on — the way a marketplace treats jobs and people.

This design system was built from 14 UI screenshots (Mobbin captures of a modern talent-marketplace web app) supplied in `uploads/`. The visual language was studied from those references and re-expressed as an **original system** for cmem viewer — no third-party logos, names, or proprietary assets are reproduced.

**Sources**
- `uploads/Braintrust Web *.png` — 14 reference screenshots (home, feed, spaces, modals, forms, messaging, talent lists). Reference only; not shipped assets.
- No codebase or Figma was provided. Everything here is authored fresh against the reference language.

---

## CONTENT FUNDAMENTALS

**Voice: a warm, direct guide.** The product speaks *to you* about *your* memory. Always second person ("Your newest observations", "Where will your attention go today?"), first person only in user-authored content.

**Casing:** Sentence case everywhere — headings, buttons, tabs, badges ("Browse memories", "Save and continue", "Looking for patterns"). Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS (except tiny meta-labels are still sentence case).

**Greeting pattern:** big, personal, punctuated — `Hi, Alex!` as a display-size page title. Friendly exclamation marks are used sparingly but deliberately ("Click the link in your email!").

**Microcopy is task-shaped, not clever.** Buttons name the outcome: "Save my availability", "View all memories", "Earn today" → for cmem: "Open timeline", "Review this week". Helper text is one plain sentence below the control ("By default, we assume you work in your location's timezone.").

**Questions as headers.** Forms ask in plain language: "What is your hourly rate for this job?" → cmem: "When did this happen?", "Who was involved?". Required state is a quiet gray "Required" suffix, not an asterisk alone.

**Emoji: only inside tinted topic badges** (💪 Freelancing, 🔥 Asking for 1:1 help) — one leading emoji, never in headings, body copy, or buttons. cmem equivalents: 🧠 Insight, 📌 Observation, 🗂 Work history.

**Numbers are celebrated quietly:** "2103 members", "Your profile is 10% complete", "38 new posts last week". Stats are inline with icons, not stat-card grids.

**Example strings (cmem voice):**
- "Hi, Alex!"
- "Welcome to cmem. You now have full access to your timeline of memories, observations, and work history. Where will your attention go today?"
- "Your newest observations"
- "Ask your memory a question..."
- "Big news from October! You shipped the viewer redesign."

---

## VISUAL FOUNDATIONS

**Canvas & surfaces.** App background is a lavender-tinted off-white (`--canvas #f6f4fb`); content lives on pure white cards (`--paper`). Depth comes from this canvas/card contrast plus hairline borders — shadows are nearly absent (cards: `--shadow-card`, barely visible; modals: one large soft `--shadow-modal`).

**Ink-first actions.** The primary button is a **black pill** with white text. Color is reserved for meaning: jade green for affirmative commits ("Save and continue"), violet for selection/toggles, red only for destruction. Secondary buttons are white pills with a hairline border; disabled is gray fill, muted text.

**Pastel tint family.** Lilac, mint, peach, butter, sky (`--lilac-100`, `--mint-100`, …) used for: feature/hero tint cards, topic badges, active nav pill (lilac-200), space banners, skill chips. Tint cards carry **oversized soft geometric arc shapes** in a darker step of the same tint (200-level), bleeding off the card corner — the system's signature decorative motif. Never gradients.

**Type.** One family — Signat (see Fonts) — at 400/500/600/700/800. Hierarchy by size jump: display 56 → h1 40 → h2 28 → h3 20 → body 16 → small 14 → micro 12. Display/headers tracked slightly tight (−0.01 to −0.02em). Body line-height 1.5.

**Radii.** Pill-forward: buttons, badges, chips, search bar, nav items are full pills (`--radius-pill`). Cards 16px, hero cards & modals 20px, inputs 12px, thumbnails 12px.

**Borders.** Hairlines everywhere (`--line-1 #e8e6f0` on white, `--line-2` on inputs). Dashed borders (`--line-dashed`) mark empty/incomplete profile sections.

**Hover / press.** Hover: background shifts one step (white → canvas; canvas → canvas-deep) or border darkens line-1 → line-2; black buttons lighten to `#2c2c32`. Press: darken + no scale tricks. Transitions 120–200ms, `--ease-out`, no bounce, no parallax.

**Layout.** Fixed left sidebar (240–280px) with icon+label pill nav; fixed top bar with centered pill search; content column max ~1180px with generous 32–48px gutters. Modals are centered white sheets (max-width ~880px, radius 20px) over a 40% ink scrim. Toasts/banners: full-width black bar (top) with white text + underlined link.

**Avatars.** Circles. Navy fill (`--navy-700`) with white initials when no photo. Sizes 32 / 40 / 56 / 96.

**Imagery.** Photographic imagery is rare and neutral-warm; UI relies on tints + arcs instead. No illustration system in the reference set — do not invent one.

**Transparency & blur.** Not used. Surfaces are opaque; the scrim is flat alpha-ink.

---

## ICONOGRAPHY

The reference uses a consistent **1.5px-stroke outline icon set** (rounded caps, ~20–24px optical size): home, briefcase, chat bubble, wallet, bell, bookmark, envelope, search, calendar, location pin, globe, link, paperclip.

- **System icons:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) via CDN — closest open match in stroke weight and roundness. Load: `<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@latest"></script>` then `lucide.createIcons()`, or copy individual SVGs. Default: 20px, `stroke-width: 1.75`, `currentColor`.
- **Brand mark:** `assets/logo.svg` (wordmark + ring mark), `assets/logo-mark.svg` — original cmem marks, simple geometry.
- **Emoji:** only as leading glyphs in topic badges (see Content Fundamentals).
- **No icon font, no PNG icons, no unicode-as-icon.**

SUBSTITUTION FLAG: reference iconography appears custom; Lucide at stroke 1.75 is a visual stand-in. Provide brand SVGs to replace.

---

## Fonts

Brand font: **Signat**, self-hosted (.otf in `assets/fonts/`) via `@font-face` in `tokens/fonts.css`, weights 400/500/600/700/800 + regular italic. **Spline Sans Mono** (Google Fonts) for timestamps/IDs.

---

## INDEX

- `styles.css` — global entry; imports everything in `tokens/`.
- `tokens/` — `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css` (radii/shadows/motion), `fonts.css`, `base.css`.
- `guidelines/` — foundation specimen cards (rendered in the Design System tab).
- `assets/` — `logo.svg`, `logo-mark.svg`.
- `components/`
  - `actions/` — **Button**, **IconButton**
  - `forms/` — **Input**, **SearchBar**, **Checkbox**, **Switch**, **ChoiceChip**
  - `display/` — **Badge**, **Avatar**, **TintCard**
  - `navigation/` — **Tabs**, **NavItem**, **TopBar**
  - `feedback/` — **Modal**, **Banner**
- `ui_kits/cmem_viewer/` — interactive recreation of the product: home, timeline, collections, search; `index.html` is click-through.
- `SKILL.md` — agent skill entry point.

<helmet>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/tokens/fonts.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/tokens/colors.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/tokens/typography.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/tokens/spacing.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/tokens/base.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/styles.css">
  <script src="_ds/cmem-viewer-design-system-f9904b75-a739-4168-bb47-c0ababbb4185/_ds_bundle.js"></script>
  <style>
    html, body { height: 100%; margin: 0; }
    body { background: var(--canvas); font-family: var(--font-sans); color: var(--ink-1); overflow: hidden; }
    a { color: var(--accent); text-decoration: none; }
    a:hover { color: var(--accent-strong); }
    body { --ink-meta: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-2) 62%, var(--ink-3)); }
    [data-askpill]:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-soft); }
    [data-stat]::after { content: attr(data-tip); position: absolute; top: calc(100% + 9px); right: 0; transform: translateY(-4px); background: var(--action-primary); color: var(--action-on-primary); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.35; padding: 7px 11px; border-radius: 9px; white-space: nowrap; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 140ms var(--ease-out), transform 140ms var(--ease-out); z-index: 90; box-shadow: var(--shadow-raised); }
    [data-stat]:hover::after { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
    [data-strip]::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
    [data-scroller]::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px; }
    [data-scroller]::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--line-2); border-radius: 4px; }
    [data-scroller]::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: transparent; }
    [data-agent-body]::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px; }
    [data-agent-body]::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--line-2); border-radius: 3px; }
    [data-stack] [data-magic] { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.82); transition: opacity 140ms var(--ease-out), transform 140ms var(--ease-out); }
    [data-stack]:hover [data-magic], [data-stack]:focus-within [data-magic] { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
    [data-dot] { border-radius: 999px; z-index: 1; }
    [data-dot]:hover, [data-dot][data-hot="true"], [data-dot]:focus-visible { z-index: 3; }
    [data-dot]:focus-visible { outline: none; }
    [data-dot] > span { outline: 3px solid transparent; transition: transform 160ms var(--ease-out), outline-color 160ms var(--ease-out); }
    [data-dot]:hover > span, [data-dot][data-hot="true"] > span, [data-dot]:focus-visible > span { transform: scale(1.5); outline-color: var(--dot-halo, var(--accent-soft)); }
    [data-dot]:active > span { transform: scale(1.25); }
    [data-dot][data-obs-type="discovery"] { --dot-halo: var(--butter-200); }
    [data-dot][data-obs-type="decision"] { --dot-halo: var(--lilac-200); }
    [data-dot][data-obs-type="feature"] { --dot-halo: var(--mint-200); }
    [data-dot][data-obs-type="refactor"] { --dot-halo: var(--sky-200); }
    [data-dot][data-obs-type="bugfix"] { --dot-halo: var(--peach-200); }
    [data-at][data-hot="true"] { border-color: var(--line-2) !important; box-shadow: var(--shadow-card) !important; transform: translateY(-1px); }
    [data-ruler]:hover [data-band] { border-color: var(--accent); }
    [data-ruler][data-scrubbing] { cursor: grabbing !important; }
    [data-ruler][data-scrubbing] [data-band] { border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft); }

    [data-stack] [data-magic]:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props="{
  "accent": { "editor": "enum", "options": ["violet", "blue", "jade", "amber", "rose", "teal"], "default": "violet", "tsType": "string", "section": "Theme" },
  "obsCardWidth": { "editor": "range", "min": 200, "max": 300, "step": 4, "default": 236, "unit": "px", "tsType": "number", "section": "Timeline" },
  "altDemo": { "editor": "boolean", "default": true, "tsType": "boolean", "section": "Alt session card" },
  "liveDemo": { "editor": "boolean", "default": true, "tsType": "boolean", "section": "Live session" },
  "askDemo": { "editor": "boolean", "default": false, "tsType": "boolean", "section": "Ask card" }
}">
class Component extends DCLogic {
  state = {
    askOpen: false, sideOpen: false, turns: [], activeProject: 'claude-mem-pro', altView: 'prompt', altMagic: null, altPhase: 'settled', altN: 6,
    mob: typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.innerWidth <= 768, sheetOpen: false,
    live: { running: false, o1: false, o2: false, o3: false, o4: false, sum: false, count: 0, playFrac: 0.02, tools: 0, queue: 0 },
    railTip: null
  };

  TYPES = [
    { t: 'feature',   color: 'var(--jade-600)' },
    { t: 'bugfix',    color: 'var(--red-600)' },
    { t: 'refactor',  color: 'var(--blue-600)' },
    { t: 'discovery', color: 'var(--amber-800)' },
    { t: 'decision',  color: 'var(--type-prompt)' }
  ];

  PROJECTS = [
    { name: 'claude-mem-pro', color: 'var(--type-prompt)' },
    { name: 'claude-mem', color: 'var(--jade-600)' },
    { name: 'imprint', color: 'var(--amber-800)' },
    { name: 'dotfiles', color: 'var(--blue-600)' }
  ];

  KINDSUM = {
    discovery: { label: 'Discoveries, distilled', meta: '2 observations', chipBg: 'var(--butter-200)', fg: 'var(--amber-800)', text: 'This session started from memory, not from scratch — the redesign direction (summary-first, card tints, the arc motif) surfaced from 14 prior sessions, and the viewer data model was confirmed before any layout work began.', cites: [{ id: 'obs-101258b', tag: '#101258 · history surfaced' }, { id: 'obs-101259b', tag: '#101259 · data model confirmed' }] },
    decision: { label: 'Decisions, distilled', meta: '1 observation', chipBg: 'var(--lilac-200)', fg: 'var(--type-prompt)', text: 'One call shaped the day: summaries become group heroes and observations demote to a small index — decided at 1:36 PM, after the old cards gave both the same weight.', cites: [{ id: 'obs-101260b', tag: '#101260 · summaries as heroes' }] },
    feature: { label: 'Features, distilled', meta: '1 observation', chipBg: 'var(--mint-200)', fg: 'var(--jade-600)', text: 'The visible change landed at 1:58 PM — sessions render as horizontal card rails, each synced to its own proportional time ruler.', cites: [{ id: 'obs-101261b', tag: '#101261 · card rails + ruler' }] },
    refactor: { label: 'Refactors, distilled', meta: '1 observation', chipBg: 'var(--sky-200)', fg: 'var(--blue-600)', text: 'The ruler ↔ strip mapping moved into useTimelineScroll at 2:11 PM — card centers interpolate, so uneven cluster widths stay honest.', cites: [{ id: 'obs-101262b', tag: '#101262 · useTimelineScroll' }] },
    bugfix: { label: 'Bugfixes, distilled', meta: '1 observation', chipBg: 'var(--peach-200)', fg: 'var(--red-600)', text: 'Closed at 2:24 PM — the viewport band no longer drifts on uneven card widths; positions recompute per frame.', cites: [{ id: 'obs-101263b', tag: '#101263 · band drift fixed' }] }
  };

  OBS = [
    { id: 101248, type: 'discovery', title: 'Current Worktree Has 79 Uncommitted Funnel-Related File Modifications', file: 'src/app/(landing)/pricing/page.tsx', time: '1:10 PM', fact: '79 uncommitted funnel-related modifications sit in the flame-jujube worktree.' },
    { id: 101249, type: 'discovery', title: 'Funnel Worktree Tracks origin/main — Funnel Branch Never Merged', file: 'src/components/cmem/FunnelPricing.tsx', time: '1:10 PM', fact: 'The worktree tracks origin/main; the funnel branch itself was never merged.' },
    { id: 101250, type: 'discovery', title: 'Working Tree Already Contains Funnel Code — Nearly Identical to Funnel Branch', file: 'src/components/cmem/FunnelPricing.tsx', time: '1:10 PM', fact: 'Local funnel code is nearly identical to the funnel branch — same components, same copy.' },
    { id: 101251, type: 'decision', title: 'Prefer Merging PR #44 over Committing the Worktree Copies', file: 'General', time: '1:11 PM', fact: 'Decision at 1:11 PM: merge the branch via PR #44, then discard the duplicate worktree copies.' },
    { id: 101252, type: 'discovery', title: 'claude-mem CLI Repo at v13.10.2 with New Release Branch Structure', file: 'Scripts/claude-mem/.git/HEAD', time: '1:11 PM', fact: 'The CLI repo sits at v13.10.2 with the new release-branch structure.' },
    { id: 101253, type: 'discovery', title: 'Working Tree Funnel Files Are Byte-Identical to Funnel Branch', file: 'src/components/cmem/FunnelPricing.tsx', time: '1:11 PM', fact: 'diff shows byte-identical funnel files between the worktree and the branch.' },
    { id: 101255, type: 'discovery', title: 'PR #44 (Funnel) Is MERGEABLE with Clean Vercel CI — Ready to Merge Now', file: 'General', time: '1:12 PM', fact: 'PR #44 is MERGEABLE with clean Vercel CI — nothing blocks the merge.' },
    { id: 101254, type: 'discovery', title: 'claude-mem CLI Branch Landscape: community-edge Active, cloud-sync-native Created Today', file: 'plans/inbox/2026-07-09-cloud-sync-native.md', time: '1:12 PM', fact: 'community-edge is active; cloud-sync-native was branched from it this morning.' },
    { id: 101256, type: 'feature', title: 'cloud-sync-native Phase 1 Complete: Schema v36 with synced_at Columns and Legacy Cursor Stamping', file: 'plans/inbox/2026-07-09-cloud-sync-native.md', time: '1:14 PM', fact: 'Schema v36 adds synced_at columns; legacy rows get a stamped cursor instead of a backfill.' },
    { id: 101257, type: 'discovery', title: 'Seed Round Fundraising Materials Found in `placid-poppyseed` Worktree', file: 'SEED-ROUND-AGENT-PLAN.md', time: '1:15 PM', fact: 'Seed-round materials live in the placid-poppyseed worktree, untouched since June.' },
    { id: 101258, type: 'discovery', title: 'Viewer Redesign History Surfaced via Memory Search', file: 'src/ui/viewer/data/viewer-types.ts', time: '1:19 PM', fact: 'Past viewer decisions (card tints, arc motif, summary-first) surfaced from 14 prior sessions.' },
    { id: 101259, type: 'discovery', title: 'Viewer Data Model and Architecture Fully Confirmed', file: 'src/ui/viewer/data/viewer-types.ts', time: '1:20 PM', fact: 'The VSession → VPrompt → VObservation join is confirmed; summaries key on memory_session_id.' },
    { id: 101260, type: 'decision', title: 'Summaries Promoted to Group Heroes — Observations Become Index Rows', file: 'src/ui/viewer/Timeline.tsx', time: '1:36 PM', fact: 'Summaries become group heroes; observations render as a small, unbolded index.' },
    { id: 101261, type: 'feature', title: 'Sessions Now Render as Horizontal Card Rails with a Time Ruler', file: 'src/ui/viewer/Timeline.tsx', time: '1:58 PM', fact: 'Each session renders one horizontal rail of observation cards under its ruler.' },
    { id: 101262, type: 'refactor', title: 'Ruler ↔ Strip Scroll Sync Extracted into useTimelineScroll', file: 'src/hooks/useTimelineScroll.ts', time: '2:11 PM', fact: 'The scroll↔ruler mapping interpolates card centers, so uneven widths stay honest.' },
    { id: 101263, type: 'bugfix', title: 'Ruler Viewport Drift Fixed for Uneven Card Widths', file: 'src/hooks/useTimelineScroll.ts', time: '2:24 PM', fact: 'The band no longer drifts when clusters change width; positions recompute per frame.' }
  ];

  typeColor(t) {
    const m = this.TYPES.find((x) => x.t === t);
    return m ? m.color : 'var(--ink-3)';
  }

  // ---------- lifecycle ----------
  componentDidMount() {
    this._timers = [];
    this._raf = 0;
    this._dragRuler = null;
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', 'light');
    this.applyProps();

    this._onDocClick = (e) => {
      const dot = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-dot]') : null;
      if (dot) {
        if (dot.closest('#sess-s1-alt')) this._stopAlt('prompt');
        this.jumpToObs(dot.getAttribute('data-dot'));
      }
    };
    this._onPointerDown = (e) => {
      const ruler = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-ruler]') : null;
      if (!ruler) return;
      if (e.target.closest('[data-dot]')) return;
      this._dragRuler = ruler;
      ruler.setAttribute('data-scrubbing', 'true');
      this.scrub(ruler, e.clientX);
      e.preventDefault();
    };
    this._onPointerMove = (e) => { if (this._dragRuler) this.scrub(this._dragRuler, e.clientX); };
    this._onPointerUp = () => {
      if (this._dragRuler) this._dragRuler.removeAttribute('data-scrubbing');
      this._dragRuler = null;
    };
    this._onAnyScroll = (e) => {
      const t = e.target;
      if (t && t.hasAttribute && t.hasAttribute('data-strip')) this.queueSync();
    };
    this._onKey = (e) => {
      const a = document.activeElement;
      const tag = (a && a.tagName) || '';
      if (e.key === '/' && tag !== 'INPUT' && tag !== 'TEXTAREA') {
        e.preventDefault();
        const i = document.getElementById('ask-input');
        if (i) i.focus();
      }
      if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        if (this.state.sheetOpen) this.setState({ sheetOpen: false });
        else if (this.state.askOpen) this.closeAsk();
      }
    };
    this._onResize = () => {
      const m = window.innerWidth <= 768;
      if (m !== this.state.mob) this.setState({ mob: m, railTip: null, sheetOpen: false });
      this.queueSync();
    };

    document.addEventListener('click', this._onDocClick);
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', this._onPointerDown);
    document.addEventListener('pointermove', this._onPointerMove);
    document.addEventListener('pointerup', this._onPointerUp);
    document.addEventListener('scroll', this._onAnyScroll, true);
    document.addEventListener('keydown', this._onKey);
    window.addEventListener('resize', this._onResize);

    // hover affinity: card ↔ ruler dot via data-hot (helmet CSS renders it, so it survives re-renders)
    this._onOver = (e) => {
      const card = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-at]') : null;
      if (card && card.id) {
        const dot = document.querySelector('[data-dot="' + card.id + '"]');
        if (dot) dot.setAttribute('data-hot', 'true');
      }
      const dotBtn = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-dot]') : null;
      if (dotBtn) {
        const target = document.getElementById(dotBtn.getAttribute('data-dot'));
        if (target) target.setAttribute('data-hot', 'true');
      }
      const tipEl = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-tip]') : null;
      if (tipEl) {
        const r = tipEl.getBoundingClientRect();
        const pos = tipEl.getAttribute('data-tip-pos') || 'right';
        const tip = { text: tipEl.getAttribute('data-tip'), pos };
        if (pos === 'above') { tip.x = r.left + r.width / 2; tip.y = r.top - 7; }
        else if (pos === 'below') { tip.x = r.left + r.width / 2; tip.y = r.bottom + 7; }
        else { tip.x = r.right + 10; tip.y = r.top + r.height / 2; }
        this.setState({ railTip: tip });
      }
    };
    this._onOut = (e) => {
      const card = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-at]') : null;
      if (card && card.id) {
        const dot = document.querySelector('[data-dot="' + card.id + '"]');
        if (dot) dot.removeAttribute('data-hot');
      }
      const dotBtn = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-dot]') : null;
      if (dotBtn) {
        const target = document.getElementById(dotBtn.getAttribute('data-dot'));
        if (target) target.removeAttribute('data-hot');
      }
      if (e.target.closest && e.target.closest('[data-tip]') && this.state.railTip) this.setState({ railTip: null });
    };
    document.addEventListener('mouseover', this._onOver);
    document.addEventListener('mouseout', this._onOut);

    // alt card: looping lifecycle demo — prompt, observations stream in, distill, summary
    this._altTimers = [];
    this._altStarted = false;
    this._altReduce = !!(window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches);
    if (this._altReduce) {
      this._altStarted = true;
      this.setState({ altView: 'summary' });
    } else if (this.props.altDemo ?? true) {
      this._altStarted = true;
      this._at(setTimeout(() => this._runAlt(), 900));
    }

    this._liveTimers = [];
    this._liveIv = null;
    this._liveStarted = false;
    if (this.props.liveDemo ?? true) {
      this._liveStarted = true;
      this._lt(setTimeout(() => this._runLive(), 1100));
    }

    this.syncAll();
    this._t(setTimeout(() => this.syncAll(), 350));
    if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) document.fonts.ready.then(() => this.syncAll());
    this._askDemoRan = !!this.props.askDemo;
    if (this.props.askDemo) this._t(setTimeout(() => this.runAsk(''), 600));
  }

  componentWillUnmount() {
    (this._timers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    (this._liveTimers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    (this._altTimers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    if (this._liveIv) clearInterval(this._liveIv);
    if (this._toolIv) clearInterval(this._toolIv);
    if (this._raf) cancelAnimationFrame(this._raf);
    document.removeEventListener('mouseover', this._onOver);
    document.removeEventListener('mouseout', this._onOut);
    document.removeEventListener('click', this._onDocClick);
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this._onPointerDown);
    document.removeEventListener('pointermove', this._onPointerMove);
    document.removeEventListener('pointerup', this._onPointerUp);
    document.removeEventListener('scroll', this._onAnyScroll, true);
    document.removeEventListener('keydown', this._onKey);
    window.removeEventListener('resize', this._onResize);
  }

  componentDidUpdate() {
    this.applyProps();
    this.syncAll();
    if (!this._altReduce && (this.props.altDemo ?? true) && !this._altStarted) {
      this._altStarted = true;
      this._runAlt();
    }
    if ((this.props.liveDemo ?? true) && !this._liveStarted) {
      this._liveStarted = true;
      this._runLive();
    }
    if (this.props.askDemo && !this._askDemoRan) {
      this._askDemoRan = true;
      this.runAsk('');
    }
  }

  _t(id) { this._timers.push(id); return id; }

  applyProps() {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-accent', this.props.accent ?? 'violet');
    const app = document.querySelector('[data-app]');
    const w = this.props.obsCardWidth ?? 236;
    if (app) app.style.setProperty('--obs-w', (this.state.mob ? Math.min(w, 212) : w) + 'px');
  }

  // ---------- ruler ↔ strip sync ----------
  cardPoints(strip) {
    const sRect = strip.getBoundingClientRect();
    const pts = [];
    strip.querySelectorAll('[data-at]').forEach((c) => {
      const r = c.getBoundingClientRect();
      pts.push({ f: parseFloat(c.getAttribute('data-at')) || 0, x: r.left - sRect.left + strip.scrollLeft + r.width / 2 });
    });
    pts.sort((a, b) => a.x - b.x);
    return pts;
  }

  fracAtX(pts, x) {
    if (!pts.length) return 0;
    if (x <= pts[0].x) return pts[0].f;
    const last = pts[pts.length - 1];
    if (x >= last.x) return last.f;
    for (let i = 0; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
      const a = pts[i], b = pts[i + 1];
      if (x >= a.x && x <= b.x) {
        const span = b.x - a.x;
        const u = span > 0 ? (x - a.x) / span : 0;
        return a.f + (b.f - a.f) * u;
      }
    }
    return last.f;
  }

  xAtFrac(pts, f) {
    if (!pts.length) return 0;
    if (f <= pts[0].f) return pts[0].x;
    const last = pts[pts.length - 1];
    if (f >= last.f) return last.x;
    for (let i = 0; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
      const a = pts[i], b = pts[i + 1];
      if (f >= a.f && f <= b.f) {
        const span = b.f - a.f;
        const u = span > 0 ? (f - a.f) / span : 0;
        return a.x + (b.x - a.x) * u;
      }
    }
    return last.x;
  }

  syncRail(rail) {
    const strip = rail.querySelector('[data-strip]');
    const band = rail.querySelector('[data-band]');
    if (!strip || !band) return;
    const pts = this.cardPoints(strip);
    if (!pts.length) { band.style.opacity = '0'; return; }
    band.style.opacity = '1';
    const f0 = this.fracAtX(pts, strip.scrollLeft);
    const f1 = this.fracAtX(pts, strip.scrollLeft + strip.clientWidth);
    const left = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, f0 * 100));
    const width = Math.max(4, Math.min(100 - left, (f1 - f0) * 100));
    band.style.left = left + '%';
    band.style.width = width + '%';
  }

  syncAll() {
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-rail]').forEach((r) => this.syncRail(r));
  }

  queueSync() {
    if (this._raf) return;
    this._raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => { this._raf = 0; this.syncAll(); });
  }

  scrub(ruler, clientX) {
    const rail = ruler.closest('[data-rail]');
    const strip = rail && rail.querySelector('[data-strip]');
    if (!strip) return;
    const rect = ruler.getBoundingClientRect();
    const f = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (clientX - rect.left) / rect.width));
    const pts = this.cardPoints(strip);
    if (!pts.length) return;
    const lo = pts[0].f, hi = pts[pts.length - 1].f;
    const x = this.xAtFrac(pts, lo + (hi - lo) * f);
    strip.scrollLeft = x - strip.clientWidth / 2;
  }

  jumpToSession(secId) {
    const sec = document.getElementById(secId);
    const scroller = document.querySelector('[data-scroller]');
    if (!sec || !scroller) return;
    const top = sec.getBoundingClientRect().top - scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top + scroller.scrollTop - 16;
    scroller.scrollTo({ top: Math.max(0, top), behavior: 'smooth' });
  }

  // ---------- jump + flash ----------
  jumpToObs(domId) {
    const el = document.getElementById(domId);
    if (!el) return;
    const rail = el.closest('[data-rail]');
    const strip = rail && rail.querySelector('[data-strip]');
    if (strip) {
      const sRect = strip.getBoundingClientRect();
      const eRect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      const target = eRect.left - sRect.left + strip.scrollLeft - (strip.clientWidth - eRect.width) / 2;
      strip.scrollTo({ left: Math.max(0, target), behavior: 'smooth' });
    }
    const scroller = document.querySelector('[data-scroller]');
    const sec = el.closest('section');
    if (scroller && sec) {
      const top = sec.getBoundingClientRect().top - scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top + scroller.scrollTop - 16;
      scroller.scrollTo({ top: Math.max(0, top), behavior: 'smooth' });
    }
    el.style.animation = 'none';
    requestAnimationFrame(() => { el.style.animation = 'dcFlash 2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 1'; });
    this._t(setTimeout(() => { el.style.animation = ''; }, 2100));
  }

  sheetJump(id) {
    this.setState({ sheetOpen: false });
    this._t(setTimeout(() => this.jumpToSession(id), 60));
  }

  altGoToObs(id) {
    this._stopAlt('prompt');
    this._t(setTimeout(() => { if (id) this.jumpToObs(id); this.syncAll(); }, 540));

  // ---------- alt card lifecycle demo ----------
  _at(id) { this._altTimers.push(id); return id; }

  _altStrip() {
    const rail = document.querySelector('[data-rail="s1b"]');
    return rail ? rail.querySelector('[data-strip]') : null;
  }

  _runAlt() {
    (this._altTimers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    this._altTimers = [];
    this._altTouched = false;
    this.setState({ altView: 'prompt', altPhase: 'stream', altN: 0, altMagic: null, railTip: null });
    this._at(setTimeout(() => {
      const strip = this._altStrip();
      if (strip) strip.scrollTo({ left: 0 });
      this.syncAll();
    }, 120));
    const land = (k) => {
      this.setState({ altN: k });
      this._at(setTimeout(() => {
        const strip = this._altStrip();
        if (strip) strip.scrollTo({ left: strip.scrollWidth, behavior: 'smooth' });
        this.syncAll();
      }, 90));
    };
    [1100, 2050, 3000, 3950, 4900, 5850].forEach((ms, i) => this._at(setTimeout(() => land(i + 1), ms)));
    this._at(setTimeout(() => this.setState({ altPhase: 'distill' }), 6900));
    this._at(setTimeout(() => {
      this.setState({ altPhase: 'settled', altView: 'summary' });
      this._at(setTimeout(() => this.syncAll(), 540));
    }, 8700));
    this._at(setTimeout(() => {
      if (!this._altTouched && (this.props.altDemo ?? true)) this._runAlt();
    }, 15400));
  }

  _stopAlt(view) {
    this._altTouched = true;
    (this._altTimers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    this._altTimers = [];
    const patch = { altPhase: 'settled', altN: 6 };
    if (view) patch.altView = view;
    this.setState(patch);
    this._t(setTimeout(() => this.syncAll(), 540));
  }

  // ---------- live session demo ----------
  _lt(id) { this._liveTimers.push(id); return id; }

  setLive(patch) { this.setState((s) => ({ live: { ...s.live, ...patch } })); }

  _runLive() {
    (this._liveTimers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    this._liveTimers = [];
    if (this._liveIv) clearInterval(this._liveIv);
    if (this._toolIv) clearInterval(this._toolIv);
    this._liveT0 = Date.now();
    this.setLive({ running: true, o1: false, o2: false, o3: false, o4: false, sum: false, count: 0, playFrac: 0.02, tools: 0, queue: 0 });
    this._toolTick = 0;
    this._toolIv = setInterval(() => {
      this._toolTick++;
      this.setState((s) => {
        if (!s.live.running) return null;
        const inc = this._toolTick % 3 === 0 ? 2 : 1;
        return { live: { ...s.live, tools: Math.min(38, s.live.tools + inc), queue: Math.min(9, s.live.queue + inc) } };
      });
    }, 700);
    const PTS = [[0, 0.02], [2.8, 0.10], [7, 0.30], [11.5, 0.55], [16, 0.75], [20, 0.78]];
    this._liveIv = setInterval(() => {
      const el = (Date.now() - this._liveT0) / 1000;
      let f = 0.78;
      if (el <= PTS[0][0]) f = PTS[0][1];
      else {
        for (let i = 0; i < PTS.length - 1; i++) {
          const a = PTS[i], b = PTS[i + 1];
          if (el >= a[0] && el <= b[0]) { f = a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * (el - a[0]) / (b[0] - a[0]); break; }
        }
      }
      this.setLive({ playFrac: f });
    }, 420);
    const land = (key, count) => {
      this.setState((s) => ({ live: { ...s.live, [key]: true, count, queue: Math.max(0, s.live.queue - 5) } }));
      this._lt(setTimeout(() => {
        const rail = document.querySelector('[data-rail="s0"]');
        const strip = rail && rail.querySelector('[data-strip]');
        if (strip) strip.scrollTo({ left: strip.scrollWidth, behavior: 'smooth' });
        this.syncAll();
      }, 80));
    };
    this._lt(setTimeout(() => land('o1', 1), 2800));
    this._lt(setTimeout(() => land('o2', 2), 7000));
    this._lt(setTimeout(() => land('o3', 3), 11500));
    this._lt(setTimeout(() => land('o4', 4), 16000));
    this._lt(setTimeout(() => {
      if (this._liveIv) { clearInterval(this._liveIv); this._liveIv = null; }
      if (this._toolIv) { clearInterval(this._toolIv); this._toolIv = null; }
      this.setLive({ sum: true, running: false, tools: 38, queue: 0 });
      this._lt(setTimeout(() => this.syncAll(), 480));
    }, 20000));
  }

  // ---------- agent ----------
  p(text) { return { key: 'p' + Math.random(), isP: true, text }; }
  bullets(items) { return { key: 'b' + Math.random(), isBullets: true, items }; }
  citeBlock(ids) {
    return {
      key: 'c' + Math.random(),
      isCites: true,
      cites: ids.map((id) => {
        const o = this.OBS.find((x) => x.id === id) || {};
        return {
          tag: '#' + id,
          title: o.title || '',
          time: o.time || '',
          dotStyle: { display: 'inline-block', width: '8px', height: '8px', borderRadius: '999px', background: this.typeColor(o.type), flexShrink: 0 },
          onClick: () => this.jumpToObs('obs-' + id)
        };
      })
    };
  }

  plan(q) {
    const L = q.toLowerCase();
    const mk = (ids, blocks) => ({
      ids,
      cand: 9 + ids.length * 4 + (L.length % 7),
      tok: 380 * ids.length + 240,
      blocks: blocks.concat([this.citeBlock(ids)])
    });
    if (/funnel|merge|pr\b|#44|worktree|pricing/.test(L)) {
      return mk([101250, 101253, 101255, 101251], [
        this.p('Yes — merge it. PR #44 has clean Vercel CI and is flagged MERGEABLE, and the funnel work sitting in your worktree is a copy of the branch, not unlanded work.'),
        this.bullets([
          'Worktree funnel files are byte-identical to the funnel branch — the merge won’t conflict with your local copies.',
          'The 79 uncommitted modifications in flame-jujube are duplicates; committing them would double-land the feature.',
          'At 1:11 PM you decided to prefer the branch merge over committing worktree copies.'
        ]),
        this.p('Open thread: after merging, prune the duplicate copies so the next session starts clean.')
      ]);
    }
    if (/sync|schema|cloud|cursor|migration/.test(L)) {
      return mk([101254, 101256], [
        this.p('cloud-sync-native is one phase in: the branch was cut this morning and schema v36 landed by 1:14 PM.'),
        this.bullets([
          'synced_at columns are live in schema v36.',
          'Legacy rows get a stamped cursor instead of a timestamp backfill — no data rewrite.',
          'The phase plan lives at plans/inbox/2026-07-09-cloud-sync-native.md.'
        ]),
        this.p('Phase 2 — the push loop — is the open thread.')
      ]);
    }
    if (/viewer|timeline|redesign|card|ruler|summary/.test(L)) {
      return mk([101258, 101259, 101260, 101261], [
        this.p('The redesign settled this afternoon: summaries lead, observations index. Here’s where it stands.'),
        this.bullets([
          'Summaries are group heroes, connected to the prompt that started the session.',
          'Observations render as horizontal rails of small cards, grouped by file like the CLI timeline.',
          'Each rail syncs to a proportional time ruler — the viewport band tracks your scroll.'
        ]),
        this.p('Next, per your 1:36 PM decision: dock the agent beside the timeline — which is what you’re looking at.')
      ]);
    }
    if (/seed|fundrais|round|invest/.test(L)) {
      return mk([101257], [
        this.p('Seed-round fundraising materials turned up in the placid-poppyseed worktree at 1:15 PM today — untouched since June.'),
        this.p('If the raise is back on, that worktree is the starting point; nothing newer exists in memory.')
      ]);
    }
    const tokens = L.split(/[^a-z0-9-]+/).filter((t) => t.length > 2);
    const scored = this.OBS.map((o) => {
      let s = 0;
      const title = o.title.toLowerCase(), fact = o.fact.toLowerCase(), file = o.file.toLowerCase();
      tokens.forEach((t) => {
        if (title.includes(t)) s += 3;
        if (fact.includes(t)) s += 2;
        if (file.includes(t)) s += 2;
        if (o.type === t) s += 2;
      });
      return { o, s };
    }).filter((x) => x.s > 0).sort((a, b) => b.s - a.s).slice(0, 4);
    if (!scored.length) {
      return {
        ids: [], cand: 0, tok: 0,
        blocks: [
          this.p('I went through all 50 observations in context and nothing matches “' + q + '” yet — either we haven’t worked on it, or memory phrases it differently.'),
          this.p('Try a file name or an exact identifier — symbols match best. Or ask about the funnel merge, cloud-sync-native, or the viewer redesign.')
        ]
      };
    }
    const ids = scored.map((x) => x.o.id);
    return mk(ids, [
      this.p('I found ' + ids.length + (ids.length === 1 ? ' memory' : ' memories') + ' that touch “' + q + '” — all from today’s work in claude-mem-pro.'),
      this.bullets(scored.map((x) => x.o.fact))
    ]);
  }

  patchTurn(key, fn) {
    this.setState((s) => ({ turns: s.turns.map((t) => (t.key === key ? fn(t) : t)) }));
  }

  _scrollThread() {
    const body = document.querySelector('[data-agent-body]');
    if (body) body.scrollTo({ top: body.scrollHeight, behavior: 'smooth' });
  }

  runAsk(raw) {
    const q = String(raw || '').trim() || 'Is the funnel PR safe to merge?';
    (this._timers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    this._timers = [];
    const plan = this.plan(q);
    this._askN = (this._askN || 0) + 1;
    const key = 'turn' + this._askN;
    const time = '2:' + (40 + this._askN) + ' PM';
    const step1 = { key: 's1', label: 'Looking through your memory…', running: true, done: false };
    const turn = { key, q, time, steps: [step1], blocks: [] };
    const wasOpen = this.state.askOpen;
    this.setState((s) => ({
      askOpen: true,
      turns: [...s.turns.map((t) => ({ ...t, steps: t.steps.map((st) => (st.running ? { ...st, running: false, done: true } : st)) })), turn]
    }));
    this._t(setTimeout(() => {
      const scroller = document.querySelector('[data-scroller]');
      if (scroller) scroller.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: wasOpen ? 'smooth' : 'auto' });
      this._scrollThread();
      const f = document.getElementById('ask-follow');
      if (f) f.focus();
      this.syncAll();
    }, wasOpen ? 60 : 380));

    const hasIds = plan.ids.length > 0;
    this._t(setTimeout(() => {
      this.patchTurn(key, (t) => {
        const st = [{ ...t.steps[0], running: false, done: true, label: hasIds ? 'Found ' + plan.cand + ' possible matches' : 'Nothing in memory matches this yet' }];
        if (hasIds) st.push({ key: 's2', label: 'Reading the ' + plan.ids.length + ' that matter most…', running: true, done: false });
        else st.push({ key: 's2', label: 'Writing back what memory does hold…', running: true, done: false });
        return { ...t, steps: st };
      });
      this._scrollThread();
    }, 850));

    if (hasIds) {
      this._t(setTimeout(() => {
        this.patchTurn(key, (t) => ({
          ...t,
          steps: [t.steps[0], { ...t.steps[1], running: false, done: true, label: 'Read ' + plan.ids.length + (plan.ids.length === 1 ? ' observation' : ' observations') + ' closely' },
            { key: 's3', label: 'Connecting what you learned…', running: true, done: false }]
        }));
        this._scrollThread();
      }, 2000));
    }

    const doneAt = hasIds ? 3050 : 1900;
    this._t(setTimeout(() => {
      this.patchTurn(key, (t) => {
        const st = t.steps.slice();
        st[st.length - 1] = { ...st[st.length - 1], running: false, done: true, label: 'Answer ready' };
        return { ...t, steps: st };
      });
    }, doneAt));

    plan.blocks.forEach((b, i) => {
      this._t(setTimeout(() => {
        this.patchTurn(key, (t) => ({ ...t, blocks: [...t.blocks, b] }));
        this._scrollThread();
      }, doneAt + 220 + i * 420));
    });
  }

    (this._timers || []).forEach(clearTimeout);
    this._timers = [];
    this._askN = 0;
    this.setState({ askOpen: false, turns: [] });
    this._t(setTimeout(() => this.syncAll(), 420));
  }

        dotStyle: { display: 'inline-block', width: '8px', height: '8px', borderRadius: '999px', background: m.color, flexShrink: 0 },
        onClick: () => this.setProject(m.name)
      })),
      onSearchKey: (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter') { this.runAsk(e.target.value); e.target.value = ''; e.target.blur(); }
      },
      onAskClick: () => {
        const i = document.getElementById('ask-input');
        this.runAsk(i ? i.value : '');
        if (i) i.value = '';
      },
      onFollowKey: (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && e.target.value.trim()) { this.runAsk(e.target.value); e.target.value = ''; }
      },
      onCloseAsk: () => this.closeAsk()
    };
  }
}

1	'use client'
2	
3	import { useRef, RefObject } from 'react'
4	import { useScroll, useTransform, MotionValue } from 'framer-motion'
5	
6	interface TimelineScrollValues {
7	  containerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>
8	  scrollYProgress: MotionValue<number>
9	
10	  // Video transforms
11	  videoOpacity: MotionValue<number>
12	  videoScale: MotionValue<number>
13	
14	  // 4 bubbles for the prompts (left side)
15	  bubble1Opacity: MotionValue<number>
16	  bubble2Opacity: MotionValue<number>
17	  bubble3Opacity: MotionValue<number>
18	  bubble4Opacity: MotionValue<number>
19	  bubble1Y: MotionValue<number>
20	  bubble2Y: MotionValue<number>
21	  bubble3Y: MotionValue<number>
22	  bubble4Y: MotionValue<number>
23	}
24	
25	/**
26	 * Scroll-linked transforms for the ContextTimeline sticky scroll section.
27	 * 4 prompt bubbles appear on the left as user scrolls.
28	 */
29	export function useTimelineScroll(): TimelineScrollValues {
30	  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
31	
32	  const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({
33	    target: containerRef,
34	    offset: ["start center", "end center"]
35	  })
36	
37	  // Video: fade in at start
38	  const videoOpacity = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 0.1], [0, 1])
39	  const videoScale = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 0.15], [1.1, 1])
40	
41	  // 4 bubbles spaced evenly through scroll
42	  // Bubble 1: 0.10 - 0.20
43	  const bubble1Opacity = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.10, 0.18], [0, 1])
44	  const bubble1Y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.10, 0.18], [40, 0])
45	
46	  // Bubble 2: 0.30 - 0.40
47	  const bubble2Opacity = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.30, 0.38], [0, 1])
48	  const bubble2Y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.30, 0.38], [40, 0])
49	
50	  // Bubble 3: 0.50 - 0.60
51	  const bubble3Opacity = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.50, 0.58], [0, 1])
52	  const bubble3Y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.50, 0.58], [40, 0])
53	
54	  // Bubble 4: 0.70 - 0.80
55	  const bubble4Opacity = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.70, 0.78], [0, 1])
56	  const bubble4Y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0.70, 0.78], [40, 0])
57	
58	  return {
59	    containerRef,
60	    scrollYProgress,
61	    videoOpacity,
62	    videoScale,
63	    bubble1Opacity,
64	    bubble2Opacity,
65	    bubble3Opacity,
66	    bubble4Opacity,
67	    bubble1Y,
68	    bubble2Y,
69	    bubble3Y,
70	    bubble4Y,
71	  }
72	}

11. public/ assets referenced by the old viewer: /cmem-viewer-logo.jpg — does it exist in public/? Anything else the old viewer references from public/?

Your final reply: numbered findings matching the list above, each with file:line citations and exact identifiers; then a "gotchas" list (max 8 bullets); then confidence + gaps. Keep it under 2500 words.

## 1. Hooks contracts

**`src/hooks/useSSE.ts`** — `useSSE()` returns `{ observations, summaries, prompts, projects, isProcessing, isConnected }` (useSSE.ts:113).
- `observations: Observation[]`, `summaries: Summary[]`, `prompts: UserPrompt[]`, `projects: string[]`, `isProcessing: boolean`, `isConnected: boolean` (useSSE.ts:6–11).
- Opens `EventSource(API_ENDPOINTS.STREAM)` = `/api/stream` (useSSE.ts:22); on error closes and reconnects after `TIMING.SSE_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS` = 3000ms (useSSE.ts:40–44; src/constants/timing.ts:7).
- Event types handled: `initial_load` (sets `projects` ONLY — historical rows come from pagination, not SSE; useSSE.ts:52–58), `new_observation`/`new_summary`/`new_prompt` (prepend to arrays), `processing_status`, `connected` (useSSE.ts:60–92). `StreamEvent` union defined at src/types/index.ts:45–56.

**`src/hooks/useStats.ts`** — `useStats()` returns `{ stats }` where `stats: Stats` starts as `{}` (useStats.ts:6, 45). Fetches `/api/stats` immediately, then polls every `TIMING.STATS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` = 60000ms (timing.ts:11) — skipped while `document.hidden`, with a catch-up fetch on `visibilitychange` (useStats.ts:31–37). Only calls `setStats` when the JSON payload changed (signature compare, useStats.ts:16–19).

**`src/constants/api.ts`** — `API_ENDPOINTS = { OBSERVATIONS: '/api/observations', SUMMARIES: '/api/summaries', PROMPTS: '/api/prompts', STATS: '/api/stats', STREAM: '/api/stream' }` (api.ts:6–12); `UI.PAGINATION_PAGE_SIZE = 50`, `UI.LOAD_MORE_THRESHOLD = 0.1` (api.ts:18–24).

**Kept data layer** — `useCloudData(): LiveState` (src/components/cloud-viewer/useCloudData.ts:203) returns `{ data, isLive, status, error, streamOk, proc: {isProcessing, queueDepth}, total, streamProjects, lastStreamObs, retry }` (useCloudData.ts:269–280); `LiveState` defined at src/components/cloud-viewer/types.ts:101–112, `ViewerData = { sessions, prompts, observations, seedNotes }` at types.ts:69–74. Note `useCloudData.ts` lives inside the cloud-viewer directory being replaced, and `types.ts` there defines its types — "keep the data layer" means keeping these two files (plus src/hooks/*).

## 2. Stats fields

Route: `/Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/src/app/api/stats/route.ts`. For a logged-in Pro user it returns exactly: `{ observationCount, summaryCount, promptCount, projects }` (route.ts:18–23), sourced from `getStats()` in src/lib/cloud/queries.ts:445–469 (SQL counts over `pro_observations`/`pro_summaries`/`pro_prompts`, `projects` = distinct project array). No session + no local worker → `401 { error: 'Session required' }` (route.ts:36–38); dev fallback proxies `http://localhost:37777/api/stats` (route.ts:6, 42).

For the desired header:
- **Observation total**: available as `observationCount` (number).
- **Session count**: NOT in /api/stats. No `sessions` field is returned by the cloud path. (The `Stats` type at src/types/index.ts:97–100 models the *local-worker* shape `{ worker?, database? }` with `database.sessions?` at index.ts:93 — it does not match the cloud payload; useCloudData casts around this at useCloudData.ts:264–267.) The current viewer derives sessions client-side by grouping observations/summaries; a new header would have to do the same or extend the route.
- **Compression %**: NOT available anywhere in this repo's stats path. Grep for compression/savings only hits landing-copy and `CLAUDE_MEM_CONTEXT_SHOW_SAVINGS_*` settings strings (src/types/index.ts:66–67, src/constants/settings.ts:13–14). No token totals are returned either.

## 3. Auth / gating

- Root middleware: `/Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/src/middleware.ts` (no repo-root middleware.ts). It rewrites `imprint.cmem.ai` hosts, then calls `updateSession()` (middleware.ts:4–19). Matcher: `"/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|api/mcp|api/pro/sync|.*\\.svg$|.*\\.png$|.*\\.jpg$|.*\\.jpeg$|.*\\.gif$|.*\\.webp$|assets/).*)"` (middleware.ts:37).
- `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`: `protectedRoutes = ['/dashboard', '/connect', '/admin']` (line 32); unauthenticated hits on those redirect to `/login?next=<path>` (lines 17–24, 93–95). `/api/admin` gets JSON 404 when unauthenticated (lines 39, 88–90). Missing Supabase env vars: protected routes still bounce to /login; public pages pass through (lines 43–54).
- **A `/dev/viewer-preview` route would be reachable without auth**: the matcher matches it, but `updateSession` only redirects paths starting with the three protected prefixes — everything else falls through to `NextResponse.next()` (line 97). No `/dev` route exists today (only `src/app/api/pro/devices`).
- `src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx` wraps dashboard/connect/admin: sets `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` (line 5), imports `./dashboard.css` (line 2, a 2209-line file), and injects `THEME_BOOT` inline script that sets `html[data-theme]` before paint from `localStorage 'cmem-theme' || 'theme' || 'system'` (line 14). A preview route outside `(authenticated)` gets neither dashboard.css nor THEME_BOOT.

## 4. Modals contract

- **ConnectModal** (src/components/dashboard/ConnectModal.tsx): props `{ open: boolean; onClose: () => void }` (line 17). Fetches `/api/pro/connect-info` once per successful open (lines 23–37). Entirely **inline-styled** (const `S`, lines 94–118) — hardcoded dark palette (`#121212` card), deliberately independent of any stylesheet ("Self-contained inline styles so it drops onto the dashboard without touching the global stylesheet", lines 8–9). **No `data-theme` usage** — it does not read the theme at all. Renders its own fixed overlay at `zIndex: 1000` (line 97). Contains `<a href="/connect">` (line 86).
- **DevicesPanel** (src/components/dashboard/DevicesPanel.tsx): props `{ open: boolean; onClose: () => void }` (line 42). Fetches `/api/pro/devices` on every open, `PATCH` for rename (lines 55, 91). Same inline-style pattern (lines 177–209), same `zIndex: 1000` overlay. No `data-theme` usage.
- Opened from src/app/(authenticated)/dashboard/page.tsx via `useState` flags; `CloudViewer` receives `onConnect`/`onDevices` callbacks (page.tsx:19–20, 103–105). `CloudViewer` props: `{ onConnect?: () => void; onDevices?: () => void; userId?: string | null }` (CloudViewer.tsx:461).
- Wrapper-CSS sensitivity: nothing — both modals are fixed-position, inline-styled, and render as siblings of CloudViewer (page.tsx:101–107). The only page-level CSS dependencies on `dashboard.css` are `.dashboard-loading` / `.loading-spinner` used by the page's loading states (page.tsx:84–85, 112; dashboard.css:2186, 2198). Both modals always render dark regardless of viewer theme.

## 5. Theme plumbing today

Writers of `html[data-theme]` (only two):
1. `THEME_BOOT` script in src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx:14 — pre-paint, reads `localStorage 'cmem-theme'` then legacy `'theme'`, else system preference; sets `'dark'|'light'`.
2. `useTheme()` in src/components/cloud-viewer/HeaderControls.tsx:47–84 — reads the same two keys (line 51, with comment that `'theme'` is the old dashboard's key), tracks `prefers-color-scheme` in system mode (lines 60–70), writes `document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', resolved)` on change (line 75), and persists explicit choices to `localStorage 'cmem-theme'` (line 80). Returns `[theme, setTheme, resolved]`. `ThemeToggle` segmented control at lines 87+.

Readers: only `src/components/cloud-viewer/cloud-viewer.css` — `html[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light }` (line 1201) and ~60 `html[data-theme="dark"]` overrides (lines 1202–1279). **`src/app/globals.css` has zero `data-theme` (and zero `prefers-color-scheme`) rules**, and no other CSS in src/ reacts to it. Landing pages are unaffected by the attribute.

## 6. Dependencies

package.json (/Users/user/Scripts/claude-mem-pro/package.json):
- `react`/`react-dom` **19.2.0** (pinned, lines 30–31); `next` **^16.0.3** (line 27); `framer-motion` **^12.23.24** (line 22) — present; `lucide-react` **^1.17.0** (line 24) — present; **no clsx/classnames**.

- Fonts: root layout loads **Spectral** and **IBM_Plex_Mono** via `next/font/google` as CSS vars `--font-spectral` / `--font-ibm-plex-mono` (src/app/layout.tsx:2, 7–20, applied on `<body>` line 69). `globals.css` self-hosts **Monaspace Radon** via `@font-face` from `/assets/fonts/monaspace-radon-var.woff2|.woff` (globals.css:3–8) — note the invalid `font-sans: swap` descriptor there (should be `font-display`). The OLD viewer additionally does runtime `@import` of Google Fonts (Fredoka, Nunito, JetBrains Mono) and Fontshare (Switzer) at cloud-viewer.css:17–18.
- Static assets: `public/` contains `assets/` (with `assets/fonts/` — monaspace files only, `assets/cmem/`, `assets/icons/`, `assets/imprint/`), plus root-level images/videos. **There is no `public/fonts/`** — self-hosted font convention is `public/assets/fonts/`. New OTFs (e.g., Signat from the design import) would go there; note the middleware matcher already excludes `assets/` paths (middleware.ts:37).

## 7. Lint / build gates

- ESLint: flat config `eslint.config.mjs` = `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals` + `eslint-config-next/typescript`, with global ignores for `.next`, `design/**`, `scripts/out/**`, `.open-next/**`, `.claude/worktrees/**`. input.content: # PLAN: Replace the cloud viewer with the "Timeline Cards" design Goal: replace `src/components/cloud-viewer/*` (mounted at `/dashboard`) with a faithful, production React implementation of the Timeline Cards design, wired to the real cloud data layer. types in `src/components/cloud-viewer/types.ts`. - `useSSE()` (`src/hooks/useSSE.ts:113`) → `{ observations, summaries, prompts, projects, isProcessing, isConnected }`. SSE `initial_load` carries **projects only** — history comes from `/api/observations|summaries|prompts` pagination. - `useStats()` (`src/hooks/useStats.ts`) → `{ stats }`; cloud payload is `{ observationCount, summaryCount, promptCount, projects }` (`src/app/api/stats/route.ts:18–23`). **No session count, no compression %** — sessions derive from `data.sessions.length`; there is no compression stat (see Phase 2 stat mapping). - Auth plumbing: `signOut` from `@/lib/auth-client` (used in old `HeaderControls.tsx:234`). - Deps available: `react` 19.2 / `next` ^16 (React Compiler ON), `lucide-react` ^1.17, `framer-motion` ^12 (avoid for this build — plain CSS animations match the design), Tailwind v4 present but the viewer is **plain CSS**. - Theme: `html[data-theme]` written pre-paint by `THEME_BOOT` (`src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx:14`, keys `cmem-theme` → legacy `theme` → system) and at runtime by the viewer's theme hook. - Modals: ``, `` — **read their CURRENT versions on `origin/main`** (redesigned in c12b3a8, newer than the analysis branch). Fixed overlays, `zIndex:1000`. - Assets: summary icons ALREADY EXIST at `public/icon-thick-{completed,investigated,learned,next-steps}.svg` (byte-equivalent artwork to `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/icon-*.svg`). Fonts go under `public/assets/fonts/` (repo convention; middleware matcher excludes `assets/`). ### Anti-patterns (repo-verified) - Do NOT read `stats.database.*` — that's the local-worker `Stats` shape; cloud payload needs the cast pattern from `useCloudData.ts:264–267`. - Do NOT name anything `useTimelineScroll` — `src/hooks/useTimelineScroll.ts` is a landing-page framer-motion hook. New ruler-sync hook = `useRailSync`, local to the viewer folder. - Do NOT put tokens on `:root` — scope to the viewer root element so nothing leaks to landing pages (old `cloud-viewer.css` put them on `:root`; it dies here). - React Compiler + `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` + `exhaustive-deps` are enforced — mirror the existing disable-comment patterns only where the old code did. - No `` without the eslint-next escape used elsewhere (`{/* eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element */}`), or use plain CSS background where cleaner. - Don't invent design values — every px/color/radius is in `DESIGN-SPEC.md`; copy, don't estimate. - Merge gate reality: **no CI, no branch protection**. `npm run lint` && `npm run build` locally + Vercel preview are the only gates — run them before merge. --- ## Phase 1 — Branch, assets, tokens, skeleton folder **Branch**: from the repo root: `git fetch origin && git switch -c viewer-timeline-cards origin/main`. Add `PLAN-viewer-timeline-cards.md` to `.git/info/exclude`. **Assets**: 1. `mkdir -p public/assets/fonts/signat` and copy the 6 OTFs from `$DESIGN/fonts/`. 2. Copy `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/logomark.webp` → `public/assets/cmem/logomark.webp`. 3. Icons: use the existing `/icon-thick-*.svg` in `public/` (verify visually identical to `$DESIGN/mirror/assets/icon-*.svg`; if any differ, overwrite from `$DESIGN`). **New folder** `src/components/timeline-viewer/`: - `tokens.css` — port `$DESIGN/tokens/*.css` **verbatim values**, restructured: all selectors scoped under `.tcv` (viewer root class), e.g. `.tcv, .tcv[data-theme="light"] { … }`, `.tcv[data-theme="dark"] { … }`, `.tcv[data-accent="blue"] { … }`. Include the `@font-face` blocks pointing at `/assets/fonts/signat/Signat-*.otf` and the Spline Sans Mono Google `@import` (top of file). Include `color-scheme` per theme. Typography/spacing/motion vars from `typography.css`/`spacing.css` go in the same scope. - `viewer.css` — port the helmet `

gh pr create --base main --head viewer-timeline-cards --title "feat(viewer): Timeline Cards redesign — summary-first session cards with time-ruler rails" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What this is

Replaces the cloud viewer at `/dashboard` wholesale with the **Timeline Cards** design (imported from the Claude Design project "Design refinement: Timeline cards"). The data layer (`useCloudData` → paginated history + SSE fold-in + stats) is kept byte-identical; everything visual and interactive is new.

## The new viewer

- **Summary-first session cards** — each wrapped session leads with a butter-tinted summary hero (arc-ring motif, Learned / Completed / Next-steps rows), prompt row beneath, and a horizontal observation rail grouped by file.
- **Proportional time rulers** — per-session rulers with typed observation dots, a viewport band synced to rail scroll by piecewise card-center interpolation, pointer scrubbing, dot↔card hover affinity, and click-to-jump with flash.
- **Ask your memory** — the header pill opens an agent card: staged progress, streamed answer blocks from the local recall engine (ported scoring), and a deduped citation rail that jumps the timeline.
- **Live sessions** — wall-clock playhead on the ruler, observations land with animation as they stream over SSE, dashed "watching your session…" placeholder, and the card converts to a summary hero when the session wraps.
- **Design system** — 4 themes (light / dark / classic-light / classic-dark) × 6 accents, scoped to the viewer root so nothing leaks to landing pages; self-hosted Signat font; sentence-case voice per the design system.
- **Mobile** — stacked header, Sessions FAB + bottom sheet.
- **Dev harness** — `/dev/viewer-preview` (404s outside development) renders the view with a deterministic fixture; `?ask=1` and `?demo=live` drive the agent and live-session choreography for verification.

## What was removed

Old `cloud-viewer` implementation (sticky-notes board, files drawer, date rail, concept chips bar, expand/collapse tree) — superseded by the design. Connect / Devices / sign-out / theme + accent live in the new gear menu. The modals' `:root` surface tokens (previously defined in the deleted `cloud-viewer.css`) are re-homed in `dashboard.css`.

Also includes the `chore: remove pm2 from dev/start scripts` commit (cherry-picked) so `npm run dev` works off main.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — zero findings in touched dirs (66 pre-existing problems elsewhere unchanged)
- `npm run build` — clean; `ƒ /dashboard`, `○ /dev/viewer-preview` in the route table
- Visual matrix: 4 themes × accents + mobile 390×844 screenshot-verified against the design references
- Interaction suites: 15/15 (rail sync, scrub, jump/flash, tooltips, sidebar, keyboard, sheet) + 19/19 (ask flow, citations, follow-ups, teardown, live land/wrap)
- `/dashboard` unauthenticated → 307 to `/login`; fonts served from `/assets/fonts/signat/`
- `grep -rn "cloud-viewer" src/` → 0
